subject: Pilot credits extension & burn-rate check-in
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits extension & burn-rate check-in

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Summary of ask: Acme wants to validate Redwood for customer-facing chat over a 2–3 week pilot. Primary success criteria: latency < 600ms p95, embedding recall > 85% on sample queries, and predictable unit economics for scale.
- Pilot cadence: you mentioned ~1.2M tokens burned in the first week (mostly generation) and an expected steady-state of ~6–10M tokens/month if we move forward.
- Pricing/qualification items we need from Acme to finalize a pilot extension & estimate production costs:
  1) Expected monthly token volume range (low/typical/high) — helps us pick batching/quantization profiles.
  2) Target unit economics (target $/1M tokens) or budget range for inference spend.
  3) Any procurement/PO timing or constraints we should be aware of.

I attached a short pilot credits proposal with two options (baseline + extended) that maps token buckets to recommended config and expected price bands. If you can confirm the token volume range and whether procurement needs a formal SOW/PO, I can route a small credits extension to cover the next two weeks while you finalize.

Proposed next steps:
- Jane: confirm monthly token ranges + preferred target $/1M tokens (or budget band)
- Marissa/Rishi: approve a pilot credits top-up (if needed) and send a brief pilot extension approval doc for signatures
- Setup a 30-min check-in next Tuesday to review extended pilot metrics

Attachments: pilot-credits-proposal.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks — I’ll standby to approve the extension once you confirm volumes.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (555) 213-9876

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot credits extension & burn-rate check-in

Hi Marissa —

Great summary, thanks. A few clarifications / numbers from our side: 

- Pilot burn so far: ~1.2M tokens in week 1 (majority generation tokens from multi-turn chat).
- Expected monthly volumes if we proceed to beta: low = 4M, typical = 8M, high = 15M tokens/month.
- Pricing target: we’re hoping to land around $150–$250 per 1M tokens for inference (this is in line with our internal budget targets; open to guidance on tradeoffs for latency vs cost).
- Procurement: Procurement wants a short SOW and a PO for anything > $10k. For the pilot extension (expected cost under $2k if you provide credits), procurement is fine with an email approval.

For the extension: can we get an additional 200k tokens in credits to continue the experiment for another two weeks? That should give us enough runway to stress the caching and test higher concurrency.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Product, Acme Corp
jane.doe@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot credits extension & burn-rate check-in

Jane —

Thanks for the detail, this is super helpful. Based on the ranges you provided: 
- Typical/expected 8M tokens/mo maps well to our "startup" profile; we can recommend the following to hit your $/1M targets:
  • If target is ~$250 / 1M: default quantization + standard batching should be fine; expect higher latency headroom but lower implementation risk.
  • If you need lower unit cost (~$150 / 1M): we’d recommend 4-bit quant + aggressive batching + prefix caching — there's a modest accuracy tradeoff for some models. We can run an eval on your sample prompts to quantify this.

Pilot credits: Approved. We will provision a 200,000-token credit top-up to the Acme pilot account today. This is intended to cover the next two weeks' burn while you finalize procurement for a potential committed pilot. I’ve attached the approval stub for your records.

Attachments: pilot-credits-approval.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

Action items after credit top-up:
- Rishi: I’ll sync with you to validate the account has the top-up and confirm the exact credit expiry date.
- Jane / Acme: confirm whether you want us to run a quick eval (2–3 days) comparing the two quantization profiles — if you want the lower $/1M target we’ll prioritize that.
- Schedule: propose Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 AM ET for a 30-min check-in to review updated metrics (latency, token burn, embedding recall).

If procurement needs a signed SOW for future spend > $10k, we can have a short template ready — happy to loop Legal/Finance once you signal go.

Thanks — I’ll confirm the credit top-up when done.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Perfect — thank you, Marissa. We received the 200k credit top-up and I confirmed with the team that it hit the project account.

We’ll take you up on the 2–3 day eval comparing 4-bit vs default quantization; I’ll upload a small prompt set to the shared Drive link and ping you when ready. Confirming the Tue 6/23 10:00 AM ET check-in — invite incoming.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Jane
